content.raw:
Short answer: Compression garments help control lymphedema by supporting tissues and reducing fluid re-accumulation. They work best when properly measured, comfortable enough to use, and combined with movement and skin care.

Clinically reviewed by Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa, Plastic, Reconstructive & Lymphedema Surgeon in Singapore. Last reviewed: August 2026. This article is for education only and does not replace personalised medical assessment.

Why fit matters

A garment that is too loose may not control swelling; one that is too tight, folded or painful can damage skin or create pressure points. Refitting is needed when limb size changes or the garment loses elasticity.

Choosing and using garments

  • Use the compression class and style prescribed by your therapist or doctor.
  • Put garments on early in the day if swelling builds later.
  • Keep fabric smooth without rolling bands.
  • Replace garments according to wear and manufacturer guidance.
  • Ask about donning aids if hand strength or flexibility is limited.

When garments are difficult

Heat, discomfort, cost, skin irritation and work demands are common barriers. Rather than stopping completely, discuss alternative fabrics, styles, liners, nighttime options or bandaging with your therapist.

Compression and surgery

Compression remains important even when LVA/LVB is considered. In selected patients, successful surgery may reduce symptoms or compression burden, but garment changes should be supervised.

Frequently asked questions

Can I buy compression online?

It is safer to be measured and prescribed, especially for established lymphedema.

Should compression hurt?

No. Pain, numbness, colour change or skin injury means the garment should be reviewed.

Do I wear compression forever?

Many patients need long-term compression, though intensity may change with treatment response.

Related surgical guide: If swelling remains persistent despite appropriate conservative care, or if recurrent cellulitis is a major issue, read LVA surgery in Singapore: lymphovenous bypass for lymphedema.
